site.name: al-Marṣad
lang.switch_help: Read this page in Arabic. The Arabic interface text is a draft awaiting review by the scholars; names, claims and sources stay as recorded.
footer.ar_draft: Arabic interface text: draft, awaiting review by the scholars
footer.ar_draft_en: Arabic interface text: draft, awaiting review by the scholars
coverage.label: Coverage: {value}
coverage.explain.stub: A stub is little more than a name, and has not been reviewed by a scholar.
coverage.explain.outline: An outline records some facts, but the record is not yet sourced.
coverage.explain.sourced: Its facts point to sources, but a scholar has not yet reviewed them.
coverage.explain.reviewed: A scholar has reviewed this record.
status.label: Status: {value}
claims.legend: Each claim shows its status. “Proposed” means put forward but not yet checked by a scholar; “accepted” means a scholar has accepted it. Where no status is recorded, no review is recorded either.
claims.ai_note: Claims that cite a story come from a document that was generated with AI. Its authenticity is unknown and scholars have not reviewed it.
facts.no_status: These facts are recorded directly on this record, not as claims, so they carry no review status.
prophet.note: Below are the stories, events and ties recorded about him, each with its own status and source.
story.banner: Draft, not yet reviewed by scholars
story.no_text: The text of this story is not yet recorded.
story.ai_note: This story comes from a document that was generated with AI. Its authenticity is unknown and scholars have not reviewed it.
details.heading: Details
details.summary: Names as recorded, who recorded what, and raw data
details.basis_heading: Basis statements recorded with the claims
date.converted: Gregorian date converted from the Hijri date ({method}); it may be off by up to {days} days
date.converted_one: Gregorian date converted from the Hijri date ({method}); it may be off by up to {days} day
date.converted_plain: Gregorian date converted from the Hijri date
date.relative: Dated relative to another event or period; no date is worked out here
home.title: al-Marṣad
home.title_suffix: The Seerah and the Companions' generation
home.lead: al-Marṣad is a working prototype: a record of the Seerah and the Companions' generation in which every person, event, place, group and story has its own page, and every claim shows how far it has been checked.
home.status_heading: What is verified, and what is not
home.status_claims: {total} claims are recorded: {proposed} proposed, {under_review} under review, {accepted} accepted.
home.status_records: Records: {stub} stub, {outline} outline, {sourced} sourced, {reviewed} reviewed, {verified} verified.
home.status_unstated: Links such as who took part in an event, or where it took place, are recorded without any status.
home.status_none: No claim on this site has been accepted by a scholar yet.
home.how_top: The top of a page says who or what it is in a few words, using only what is recorded.
home.how_claims: Below that come the claims, each with its status and its source.
home.how_details: At the bottom, Details gives the names as recorded, who recorded each claim, and the raw identifiers and data.
home.names_note: Names are shown in a popular spelling. The scholarly spelling is under Details on each page.
home.plain_note: With JavaScript on, the Plain words switch at the top of each page shows plain English in place of an Arabic term wherever the glossary records a plain wording, and leaves out Arabic terms given in brackets after their English. Your choice is kept on this device only.
home.ar_note: This is the Arabic interface, a draft awaiting review by the scholars. It covers the reader pages. Names, claims, sources and story texts are shown as recorded, in English where no Arabic is recorded, and the views listed below are in English only for now.
search.title: Search names
search.label: Name of a person, event, place, group or story
search.help: Type part of a name, in English or in Arabic script. Capitals, spelling marks, al- and b., bin or ibn make no difference, and similar spellings are listed too.
search.nojs: Searching needs JavaScript, which is off or not available in this browser. Instead, every name is listed below from A to Z, and your browser's “Find in page” can look through the list.
search.scope: A search looks through the names of {people}, {events}, {places}, {groups} and {stories}, in their popular and their scholarly spellings. {arabic} in Arabic script so far; other names are matched to Arabic by sound.
search.unverified: The corpus is small and none of it has been reviewed by scholars yet. A name that cannot be found has most likely not been added yet: its absence here says nothing about whether the sources mention it.
search.partly_verified: The corpus is small, and only {accepted} of its {total} claims have been accepted by scholars so far. A name that cannot be found has most likely not been added yet: its absence here says nothing about whether the sources mention it.
search.empty_next: Try another spelling or a shorter part of the name, or browse the lists linked above.
search.similar_note: Similar spellings sound like what you typed once vowels and spelling marks are set aside. Check that each one is the person, event or place you mean.
search.arabic_note: Few names are recorded in Arabic script yet, so a search in Arabic is matched to the sound of each name's English spelling. A result under “Similar spellings” does not mean that an Arabic name is recorded for it.
search.more: Showing the first {n}. Type more of the name to narrow the list.
glossary.title: Glossary of Arabic terms
glossary.lead: Terms that appear in this site's labels. A definition is shown only where the project's own documents already give one, quoted as written; scholars have not reviewed these wordings.
glossary.none_defined: No term has a definition in the project's documents yet.
glossary.needed_lead: These terms appear in the data but have no definition in the project's documents yet.
glossary.plain_lead: Where the repository pairs a term with a plain English wording, that wording is shown with its source. The Plain words switch (with JavaScript) shows it in place of the term on every page.
plain.label: Plain words
plain.help: Shows plain English in place of Arabic terms, where the glossary records a plain wording
door.views_lead: Also built from the same graph:
door.discover.title: Discover
door.discover.lead: Stories first: short narratives from the Seerah, each followed by the people in it and how far each claim has been checked.
door.study.title: Study
door.study.lead: People, groups and events in time order, with the evidence first: each link opens a page at its claims, their status and their sources.
door.study.page_lead: Events in time order, then every person and group. Each link opens the page at its evidence: the claims, each with its status and its source. The short summary sits just above it.
door.research.title: Research
door.research.lead: Sources and data: who recorded each claim, what is disputed or missing, every record with its raw data, and the whole graph to download.
door.research.page_lead: Who recorded the claims, what they cite, what is disputed or missing, and the data itself. Each record opens at its evidence, and links its own raw data.
hub.heading: Every view of the graph
hub.lead: All of these show the same graph and the same claims, with the same status labels.
hub.reader.name: Reader pages
hub.reader.desc: One plain page for every record, complete without JavaScript:
hub.study.name: Study
hub.study.desc: Events in time order, then people and groups, each opened at its evidence.
hub.research.name: Research
hub.research.desc: Sources, open questions, every record with its raw data, and downloads.
hub.experiments.desc: Pages made while the project was being designed, kept as they were.
hub.view.observatory.name: Observatory
hub.view.observatory.desc: The whole graph as one interactive picture, arranged by relationship, time, place or story.
hub.view.timeline.name: Timeline
hub.view.timeline.desc: Events on a time axis from their recorded dates; anything undated is listed, not placed.
hub.view.lifelines.name: Life lines
hub.view.lifelines.desc: Each person's life as a line, joined to others at the events they shared, by date or by age.
hub.view.map.name: Map
hub.view.map.desc: Places and events on a map from their recorded locations; anything unlocated is listed, not placed.
hub.view.learn.name: Learning paths
hub.view.learn.desc: Guided paths through the graph, step by step, with your progress kept on this device.
hub.view.ask.name: Ask the graph
hub.view.ask.desc: Ask a question in plain words; the answer lists the claims behind it, each with its status.
study.events_note: Each event is placed by the earliest day recorded for it and shown with its date as recorded. Events with no recorded date come after, unplaced.
research.sources_lead: Who recorded the claims and links in the graph, and which works the claims cite. Each claim shows its own status on its page.
research.no_questions: No open question or gap is recorded yet.
research.download.graph.note: Every record, claim and status on this site, in one file.
research.download.external_ids.note: Proposed by a matching tool and not reviewed: candidates, not identities.
research.entity_ttl: Each record's own Turtle is linked under Details on its page, and in the list below.
research.iris: Every record has a stable identifier (IRI) under https://w3id.org/marsad/id/, and its page address is made from that identifier, never from a name.
research.licence: Text and data are under CC BY-SA 4.0; the tables of identifiers are under CC0.
research.records_note: A to Z by type. Each name opens the page at its evidence; Turtle is the record's raw data.
evidence.heading: Evidence
evidence.lead: Each claim about {name}, with its status and its source.
evidence.none: No claim about {name} is recorded yet.
thread.open_note: Every event, story and tie recorded here, in order. Pick anyone who shares a moment to follow the thread on to them.
thread.lead.one: {n} moment. Pick anyone who shares it to follow the thread on to them.
thread.lead.other: {n} moments. Pick anyone who shares a moment to follow the thread on to them.
thread.group_stories: Stories, in reading order (no date is recorded for them)
thread.note: Each moment links to its page, where every claim shows its source.
thread.unreviewed: Nothing on this thread has been reviewed by a scholar yet.
thread.failed: The thread could not be loaded. Every link on this page still works.
thread.title: The thread of {name}
external.heading: Possible matches elsewhere
external.lead: Records in other databases that a matching tool proposed as possibly the same. A proposal is not a finding: until someone reviews it, it may be wrong.
external.label: (named there: {value})
experiments.title: Earlier prototypes
experiments.lead: Pages made while the project was being designed, before its records were joined into one graph. They are kept as they were built, as a record of how the site came about.
experiments.banner: Earlier prototypes: they read their own copies of the data, which may differ from the graph, and nothing on them has been reviewed by scholars.
experiments.note: Each prototype needs JavaScript and was made for a large screen. Only their web fonts are left out, so that they load nothing from other sites.
experiments.copy_note: An earlier prototype of al-Marṣad, kept as it was built (only its web fonts are left out). Nothing on it has been reviewed by scholars.
experiments.demo.name: One event, all the way down (the Hijrah demo)
experiments.demo.desc: One event from the Hijrah, the shelter in Ghār Thawr, modelled down to its report and chain, in a picture that moves between network, generations and map.
experiments.generation1.name: The first generation
experiments.generation1.desc: The Prophet ﷺ and 35 Companions as a network, joined by companionship, kinship and six events from 2 to 11 AH.
experiments.generation1.at_scale.name: At scale
experiments.generation1.at_scale.desc: The same 35 people inside a field of anonymous points standing for those not yet recorded. No point stands for a named person.
experiments.generation1.wider_network.de: About 100 seed incidents: pick a person and follow their thread. The thread on the person pages comes from here.
experiments.stories50.name: 50 Stories, connected
experiments.stories50.desc: The 50 Stories on one dial, with everyone they name. The stories come from a document generated with AI; its authenticity is unknown.
